open1.text: This is a simulated benchmark: two alloy discovery campaigns, replayed for a whole year in a digital twin of our planned automated lab.
open1.spoken: This is a simulated benchmark: two alloy discovery campaigns, replayed for a whole year in a digital twin of our planned automated lab.
open1.phonemes: ðɪs ɪz ɐ sˈɪmjʊlˌeɪɾᵻd bˈɛntʃmɑːɹk: tˈuː ˈælɔɪ dɪskˈʌvɚɹi kæmpˈeɪnz, ɹˈiːpleɪd fɚɹə hˈoʊl jˈɪɹ ɪn ɐ dˈɪdʒɪɾəl twˈɪn ʌv ˌaʊɚ plˈænd ˈɔːɾəmˌeɪɾᵻd lˈæb.

open2.text: Some of it comes from real sources: the lab's design and its 3-D model, footage from our own atomizer, the search spaces in the two proposals, and published prices. Everything else is simulated: every alloy, every measurement, and every result.
open2.spoken: Some of it comes from real sources: the lab's design and its three D model, footage from our own atomizer, the search spaces in the two proposals, and published prices. Everything else is simulated: every alloy, every measurement, and every result.
open2.phonemes: sˌʌm ʌv ɪt kˈʌmz fɹʌm ɹˈiːəl sˈɔːɹsᵻz: ðə lˈæbz dɪzˈaɪn ænd ɪts θɹˈiː dˈiː mˈɑːdəl, fˈʊɾɪdʒ fɹʌm ˌaʊɚɹ ˈoʊn ˈæɾəmˌaɪzɚ, ðə sˈɜːtʃ spˈeɪsᵻz ɪnðə tˈuː pɹəpˈoʊzəlz, ænd pˈʌblɪʃt pɹˈaɪsᵻz. ˈɛvɹɪθˌɪŋ ˈɛls ɪz sˈɪmjʊlˌeɪɾᵻd: ˈɛvɹi ˈælɔɪ, ˈɛvɹi mˈɛʒɚmənt, ænd ˈɛvɹi ɹɪzˈʌlt.

dag1.text: Each campaign is a function network: a chain of steps, where each step's results feed the next. BOFN, Bayesian optimization over function networks, models every step, not just the final score.
dag1.spoken: Each campaign is a function network: a chain of steps, where each step's results feed the next. B O F N, Bayesian optimization over function networks, models every step, not just the final score.
dag1.phonemes: ˈiːtʃ kæmpˈeɪn ɪz ɐ fˈʌŋkʃən nˈɛtwɜːk: ɐ tʃˈeɪn ʌv stˈɛps, wˌɛɹ ˈiːtʃ stˈɛps ɹɪzˈʌlts fˈiːd ðə nˈɛkst. bˈiː ˈoʊ ˈɛf ˈɛn, beɪˈiːʒən ˌɑːptɪmᵻzˈeɪʃən ˌoʊvɚ fˈʌŋkʃən nˈɛtwɜːks, mˈɑːdəlz ˈɛvɹi stˈɛp, nˌɑːt dʒˈʌst ðə fˈaɪnəl skˈɔːɹ.

dag2.text: For aluminium, the lab makes each alloy's powder itself, then prints it and checks every build.
dag2.spoken: For aluminum, the lab makes each alloy's powder itself, then prints it and checks every build.
dag2.phonemes: fɔːɹ ɐlˈuːmɪnəm, ðə lˈæb mˌeɪks ˈiːtʃ ˈælɔɪz pˈaʊdɚɹ ɪtsˈɛlf, ðˈɛn pɹˈɪnts ɪt ænd tʃˈɛks ˈɛvɹi bˈɪld.

dag3.text: For copper, a one-hour corrosion screen ranks the DED deposits, and thirty days in seawater come before a utility is known.
dag3.spoken: For copper, a one-hour corrosion screen ranks the D E D deposits, and thirty days in seawater come before a utility is known.

dag4.text: Both campaigns share one lab. From here on, each step is an icon that lights up while it runs.
dag4.spoken: Both campaigns share one lab. From here on, each step is an icon that lights up while it runs.
dag4.phonemes: bˈoʊθ kæmpˈeɪnz ʃˈɛɹ wˈʌn lˈæb. fɹʌm hˈɪɹ ˈɔn, ˈiːtʃ stˈɛp ɪz ɐn ˈaɪkɑːn ðæt lˈaɪts ˌʌp wˌaɪl ɪt ɹˈʌnz.

fig1.text: Best so far is the highest utility of any alloy tested yet. The dotted line is the target: the best reference alloy's score on the twin's synthetic alloy model. One random design in twelve beats it, so reaching it shows how fast a lab tests its first alloys, not a discovery.

fig2.text: Against money, the same curve shows what the progress cost. The grey dashed curve is the conventional lab: the same optimizer through partner and core facilities, ordering its metal as it goes.

fig3.text: Where each first reaches the target, the median over the runs, gives the acceleration factor: here 220 days over 116, or 1.9 times. Money gives the cost ratio the same way.

res1.text: Each panel is one policy: twelve one-year runs in the automated lab, twelve three-year runs in the conventional one. BOFN finished highest on aluminium. On copper, tiered CALPHAD screening finished ahead of BOFN with blend screening, 0.68 against 0.58 over 24 seeds, and plain BOFN did no better than random.

With both labs ordering as they go, aluminium's factor is 1.2.

take2.text: To get there, with the equipment included, the automated lab cost 2.0 times as much for aluminium, and 1.15 times for copper; counting only what the campaigns spent, 0.6 and 0.4 times. With the equipment, it costs less only for copper, and only if outside users rent its idle hours, which this model assumes and does not show.

take3.text: Against a conventional lab run by a metallurgist's rules of thumb, the automated lab is no faster on aluminium, at 2.6 times the operating cost, and 2.2 times faster on copper.

note1.text: Everything here is simulated: the alloys, the results, and every measurement, with modelled noise not yet calibrated on the lab's instruments. Station times, fees and schedules, the stock on the shelf, the atomizer's failure rate and yield, and who staffs the lab are assumptions. It shows how the lab's design and its optimizer interact in a model, not what the real lab will find.
